history: Kyalami Grand Prix Circuit, located in Midrand, Gauteng, South Africa, has a rich motorsport history dating back to the 1960s. The original circuit hosted numerous Formula One South African Grand Prix races, attracting legendary drivers and teams. Following a period of decline and eventual redevelopment, the circuit was brought back to FIA Grade 2 standards in 2014 and has since hosted a variety of international and national motorsport events. The modern Grand Prix layout (4.522km) is a challenging configuration, having hosted rounds of the World Endurance Championship, the Intercontinental GT Challenge, and various national championships. While F1 has yet to return to the modern circuit, Kyalami remains a prominent venue in the South African motorsport landscape.
atmosphere: Standing on the main straight at Kyalami as the cars thunder towards Crowthorne Corner is an experience that tingles the senses. The roar of the engines echoes off the nearby hills, creating a visceral symphony of speed. The vibrant colours of the grandstands, the smell of burning rubber, and the palpable excitement of the crowd all combine to create an electrifying atmosphere. The energy is infectious, a potent mix of South African passion for motorsport and the anticipation of witnessing high-speed battles unfold on this iconic circuit.
trackCharacter: The Grand Prix layout at Kyalami is a blend of high-speed straights, flowing corners, and challenging technical sections. The elevation changes, particularly through the Esses and down to Leeukop, add another layer of complexity. The circuit rewards drivers who can find a good rhythm and carry speed through the corners, while also demanding precision and control under braking. It is a circuit that favors cars with good aerodynamic balance and strong engine performance, making it a thrilling test for both drivers and machines.

famousCorners.name: Crowthorne Corner
famousCorners.description: A fast, sweeping right-hander at the end of the main straight, Crowthorne is a crucial corner for setting up an overtaking opportunity into Sunset. It is also one of the most iconic corners on the circuit.
famousCorners.challenge: Carrying maximum speed through the corner without running wide and losing momentum for the following straight.

famousCorners.name: Sunset Bend
famousCorners.description: A tight right-hander that immediately follows Crowthorne, Sunset provides a great overtaking opportunity. The braking zone is bumpy and unforgiving.
famousCorners.challenge: Braking late and accurately while defending the inside line from rivals.

famousCorners.name: The Esses
famousCorners.description: A series of fast, flowing corners that test the car's balance and the driver's precision. Maintaining momentum is key through this section.
famousCorners.challenge: Stringing together the perfect line through the Esses while managing the car's weight transfer.

famousCorners.name: Leeukop
famousCorners.description: A long, downhill left-hander that requires commitment and bravery. It's a corner where time can be easily gained or lost.
famousCorners.challenge: Holding a tight line at high speed while managing tire wear and maintaining stability.

famousCorners.name: Ingwe
famousCorners.description: A double apex right hander. The second apex is often blind, making the entry tricky. This leads into the final sector.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining speed through both apexes, and avoiding running wide onto the kerbs.

overtakingSpots: The braking zone for Turn 4 (after the Esses)
historySnippets: The circuit has undergone several major redesigns throughout its history.
Kyalami hosted the South African Grand Prix for many years.
The 1977 South African Grand Prix was marred by the tragic death of Tom Pryce.
The circuit was purchased by Porsche South Africa CEO Toby Venter in 2014.
Kyalami hosted a round of the World Endurance Championship in 2020.
weatherNotes: Kyalami experiences a subtropical highland climate, with warm summers and mild winters. Rainfall is common, particularly during the summer months, which can make for unpredictable racing conditions. Afternoon thunderstorms are a frequent occurrence, potentially leading to wet or drying track conditions during a race.
drivingAdvice: To master the Grand Prix layout at Kyalami, focus on carrying speed through the flowing corners and maintaining a smooth driving style. Be precise with your braking points, especially into Sunset and the braking zones after the Esses. Tire management is crucial, particularly during longer races, so avoid overdriving the car in the early stages. The elevation changes and blind crests require careful attention, so study the track map and use your track time wisely to learn the circuit's nuances.
famousRaces: 1982 South African Grand Prix: Alain Prost won a chaotic race that saw several lead changes and numerous retirements.
1993 South African Grand Prix: Alain Prost secured victory in his Williams-Renault, marking his return to F1 after a year's sabbatical.
2019 9 Hours of Kyalami: A thrilling endurance race that saw Porsche take victory after a hard-fought battle with Audi and BMW.
localCulture: The Gauteng province, where Kyalami is located, is a vibrant hub of South African culture. The region is known for its diverse population, rich history, and thriving arts scene. The local cuisine is a delicious blend of African, European, and Asian influences, with dishes such as biltong (dried cured meat), bunny chow (a hollowed-out loaf of bread filled with curry), and braai (barbecue) being popular choices. Paddock life at Kyalami is characterized by a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, with teams and drivers often interacting with local fans and sharing their passion for motorsport.
